method: Independent model lexical-number review against exact retained English Wiktionary and Spanish Wiktionary meanings; not native-human certification. No application data changed.
context: The selected human-collective reading means persons collectively. Gente is grammatically singular and gentes is grammatically plural in Spanish; both can use English people. English peoples instead selects distinct peoples/nations or ethnic communities, not merely additional individual persons.
correction: Bind a selected English plural override to the exact gente noun record, sense 0, English people human-collective reading and explicit source plural-of-gente form. Preserve original Spanish plural/feminine tags; do not let generic AGID people→peoples overwrite this reviewed reading.
limitations: This is a safe selected ordinary human-collective reading, not a declaration that gentes can never denote nations or distinct communities.
Retained Spanish sense 1 Pueblo is a separate possible collective/community sense, which would require its own exact source/meaning review if peoples is intended.
Do not make a global English people→people rule: pueblo→peoples can be legitimate for distinct nations/ethnic communities.
Do not change singular person→people, or other unrelated noun paradigms.
